channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: AirTag in checked luggage: TSA rules and sharing it with your airline
item.description: An AirTag is allowed in checked and carry-on bags in the US, because its small coin battery stays inside the tracker, and since iOS 18.2 you can send its location to more than 50 airlines when a bag goes missing.

item.title: Emulators on iPhone explained: Delta, RetroArch and what's allowed
item.description: Since April 2024 Apple has let retro game emulators like Delta and RetroArch into the App Store, but the apps come without games, and playing copies of games you download from the web is usually against copyright law.

item.title: iPhone Duo face unlock vs Face ID: how the new option differs
item.description: The iPhone Duo's new face unlock in the iOS 27.3 beta uses an ordinary front camera instead of Face ID's depth sensors, so Apple keeps it to the Lock Screen, asks for Touch ID again after about 45 minutes and warns that it's less secure than Touch ID or Face ID.

item.title: 10 new graphic design apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Ten design and drawing apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Graphics & Design charts this week, from the 3D renderer RAYS to Wallmix's wallpapers and widgets.

item.title: 10 new music apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These music apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Music charts this week, from chord and synth instruments to metronomes and retro music players for your Apple Music library.

item.title: 10 new photo and video apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These photo and video apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Photo & Video charts this week, from RAW editors and film looks to a photo booth and a camera trick that gets kids to look at the lens.

item.title: 10 new productivity apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These productivity apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Productivity charts this week, from a 3D CAD app to focus timers, planners and a family chore chart.

item.title: 10 new weather apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Ten weather apps that came out in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Weather charts this week, from Snow Day Radar's snow day odds to SkyWX's radar and alerts.

item.title: 6 new education apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Six learning apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Education charts this week, from the CrowCards flashcards to a plant explorer.

item.title: 7 new navigation and GPS apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Seven navigation apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Navigation charts this week, from a trail ride tracker to a speed camera warner.

item.title: 7 new travel apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Seven travel apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Travel charts this week, from Watchmen's camera map to an offline voice translator.

item.title: 8 new entertainment apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Eight entertainment apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Entertainment charts this week, including Jitless for PC games and Roku's new official app.

item.title: 8 new utility apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These utility apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Utilities charts this week, most of them made for the foldable iPhone Duo, from Safari extensions to desk clocks and a fold counter.

item.title: 9 new health and fitness apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These health and fitness apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Health & Fitness charts this week, from lifting logs and a calorie tracker to Apple Watch tools for naps, counting and blood oxygen.

item.title: 9 new lifestyle apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These lifestyle apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Lifestyle charts this week, from a retro fridge wallpaper to a phone lock for nights out.

item.title: Android Fast Switch may let you use one SIM on two phones
item.description: Code in a recent update of Google's SIM Manager app points to Android Fast Switch, which would move your mobile service to whichever of your phones you unlock, according to an APK teardown by Android Authority. Google hasn't confirmed it.

item.title: Beyond Notes markdown notes app for Mac, iPhone and iPad
item.description: Beyond Notes is a new markdown notes app for iPhone, iPad and Mac that shows headings, lists and tables as a finished page while you type, and saves every note as a plain text file in your own iCloud Drive. Your first 50 notes are free.

item.title: Budget apps that connect to your bank vs offline trackers explained
item.description: A budget app either reads your bank and card transactions through a link, as Gemini now can through Google Wallet, or works only with what you type in, and that choice decides how much it sees, where your numbers are stored and what you give up in return.

item.title: ChatGPT travel booking may come: OpenAI hires a travel team
item.description: OpenAI is hiring engineers to build travel into ChatGPT, with a job listing for screens that compare stays and transport using live prices and availability, Skift reports. OpenAI hasn't announced a travel feature.

item.title: Copper landline switch off: what replaces your home phone and alarm
item.description: AT&T and Verizon have started switching off old copper landlines area by area, and their replacements keep your number but run on home power with a backup battery, so alarms, medical alert devices and cordless phones need a check before your date.

item.title: Crate Apple Music library app shows your albums as records
item.description: Crate is a new $14.99 app that turns your Apple Music library into a room of records, picking albums back up at the song and second you stopped. It was #73 in paid Music apps on the US App Store on 16 November.

item.title: Create My Widget on Pixel 10 and 11: how to get it early
item.description: Google's Create My Widget app, which builds a home screen widget from a description you type, can now be installed early through a beta on the Google Play Store. It works on the Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series, not the Pixel 10a.

item.title: Dia browser for iOS and Android coming in 2027, Arc shuts down 22 December
item.description: The Browser Company's CEO Josh Miller said on 15 November that its Dia browser will come to iPhone and Android in 2027. Meanwhile its older Arc browser loses its AI features on 23 November and shuts down on 22 December.

item.title: Duo Keyboard app lets iPhone Duo owners resize and split the keyboard
item.description: Duo Keyboard is a new $2.99 keyboard for the iPhone Duo that sits lower on the closed phone, so more of your message stays in view, and splits between your thumbs on the open screen. It was #98 in paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 16 November.

item.title: FourTrack: a four-track cassette recorder app for iPhone, iPad and Mac
item.description: FourTrack lets you record a song in four layers like an old tape machine: play one part, then record the next on top of it. It came out on 13 November for $5.99 and was #87 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 16 November.

item.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra design leak: raised camera plateau with three cameras
item.description: Leaker Ice Universe posted a drawing he calls the real design of the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra: a raised camera area with three rear cameras. Samsung hasn't confirmed it.

item.title: Gemini models explained: Flash-Lite, Hydrogen, Pro, Argon and Carbon
item.description: The Gemini app now lists five models, and which ones you can pick depends on your plan: without a Google AI plan you get Auto or Flash-Lite, AI Plus adds Hydrogen, AI Pro adds Pro and Argon, and only AI Ultra gets Carbon.

item.title: Gemini voice change: 66 new regional accents in the Gemini app
item.description: The Gemini app is getting 66 new voices tuned to local accents and rhythm, across US, UK and Indian English, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian and Korean. Google started rolling them out on Android and iPhone on 16 November.

item.title: Google Maps itinerary planner: Ask Maps now plans whole trips
item.description: Ask Maps, the Gemini-powered chat inside Google Maps, can now build a plan for a day out or a trip of several days, with numbered stops on the map and live details for each one. It started rolling out on Android and iPhone on 16 November.

item.title: HOURS shift tracker app logs your work time without an account
item.description: HOURS is a simple iPhone app for writing down when a shift starts and ends and how long your break was; it shows the net time for each shift and your totals. It costs $1.99 and was #43 among paid Business apps on the US App Store on 16 November.

item.title: Instagram Amazon affiliate links now work in Reels and feed posts
item.description: Instagram creators in the US who are in Amazon's influencer program can now tag Amazon products with their affiliate link right in Reels and feed posts, not only in stories, DMs and bios. Meta announced it on 16 November.

item.title: iPhone 20 Pro design rumors: iPhone Air glass curved on all four sides
item.description: Leaker Fixed Focus Digital says next year's iPhone 20 Pro will use the iPhone Air's glass, curved more strongly on all four sides. Apple hasn't confirmed the design or the name.

item.title: Lullwind lullaby app for iPhone: a wind-up music box for babies
item.description: Lullwind is a new iPhone and iPad app that plays lullabies on a wind-up timer, so the music slows down and fades out by itself. Parents can add rain or white noise and record a lullaby in their own voice.

item.title: One UI 9.5 leaked features: Galaxy Claw AI agent, Bixby Memory and more
item.description: Leaks and app teardowns point to an AI agent called Galaxy Claw in Samsung's One UI 9.5 that could use apps such as Calendar, Gmail, Messages and Phone for you. 9to5Google collected what has leaked so far; Samsung hasn't announced any of it.

item.title: Open Screen Sharing app controls your Mac from iPhone and iPad
item.description: Open Screen Sharing is a remote desktop app for iPhone and iPad that connects to a Mac's built-in screen sharing, and also to VNC and RDP computers. It was #91 in Utilities on the US App Store's paid chart on 16 November.

item.title: Outlook outage cause: Microsoft blames a hidden bug from July
item.description: Microsoft says the Outlook outage of 12 and 13 November came from a bug that had sat unnoticed in its network servers since July. A jump in traffic and fewer working servers set it off.

item.title: Paint Anytime: a drawing app for Apple Watch with layers
item.description: Paint Anytime lets you draw and paint on your Apple Watch, with brushes, layers, a lasso and a fill tool. It was #28 in Graphics & Design on the US App Store's paid chart on 16 November.

item.title: RaceCut: song to video app turns your track into a singing race
item.description: RaceCut, a new free iPhone app, turns a song into a short vertical video where marbles, balls or a band race, and whoever leads is the one singing. It was #94 in Photo & Video on the US App Store's free chart on 16 November.

item.title: Ripple Player: Apple Music record player app plays whole albums
item.description: Ripple Player, a new $4.99 iPhone app, shows the full albums in your Apple Music library as records on a shelf and plays each one from the first track to the last, with no shuffle or playlists. It was #19 in Music on the US App Store's paid chart on 16 November, its first day out.

item.title: Samsung Wallet QR code payments with Visa start in Australia and Singapore
item.description: Galaxy phone owners in Australia and Singapore can now pay with a Visa card in Samsung Wallet by scanning a shop's QR code, Visa and Samsung announced on 16 November. More Asia Pacific countries are to follow over the next few quarters.

item.title: Siri AI usage limits: iCloud+ 200 GB and up raise the daily limit
item.description: Siri AI and some Apple Intelligence features have a daily usage limit on each device, and with iOS 27.3 an iCloud+ plan of 200 GB or more raises it. Apple's support page lists up to 2x for 200 GB, 5x for 2 TB, 10x for 6 TB and 20x for 12 TB.

item.title: SkyVoxel: 3D weather radar app shows storms you can spin and slice
item.description: SkyVoxel, a new $2.99 iPhone and iPad app, turns US Doppler radar from NOAA's NEXRAD network into a 3D model of a storm that you can rotate, tilt and cut through. It was #14 in Weather on the US App Store's paid chart on 16 November.

item.title: TidyList: YouTube playlist organizer finds duplicates and deleted videos
item.description: TidyList is a new web tool that lets you sort, filter and bulk-move videos between your YouTube playlists after signing in with Google. It also flags duplicate, private, removed and hidden videos so you can clear them in one go.

item.title: TruePrompter: teleprompter app that floats over your camera, $9.99
item.description: TruePrompter shows your script on top of the camera or any other app on iPhone and iPad and scrolls along as you speak. It costs $9.99 once, with no subscription, and was #76 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 16 November.

item.title: Uber robotaxi in Las Vegas: Zoox rides now in the Uber app
item.description: Amazon's Zoox robotaxis can now pick up Uber riders in Las Vegas, starting 16 November. You can't book one directly yet: riders who request UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Comfort Electric or Wait & Save may be matched with a Zoox.

item.title: Facebook additional profiles going away: deleted after December 14
item.description: Meta is ending the extra profiles you could add under one Facebook account, and every additional profile will be permanently deleted after December 14, 2026. Your main profile and business Pages stay as they are.

item.title: Roku app for iPhone: free movies and live TV with no account
item.description: Roku has put out a new app, Roku App (Official), for watching free movies, shows and more than 500 live TV channels on iPhone and iPad without an account, subscription or credit card. It came out on 10 November and was #73 among free Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: AI agents shopping for you: what ChatGPT, Gemini and Meta Muse can do
item.description: Since this week, ChatGPT's Dots agents can buy things for US Pro subscribers once you approve each purchase, Meta's Muse can phone US businesses for paying users, and Gemini can read your Google Wallet spending without touching your money; some sellers, Amazon and United Airlines among them, block agents.

item.title: aire breathwork app for iPhone picks sessions from your health data
item.description: aire is a new breathing exercise app for iPhone and Apple Watch that suggests a session for relaxation, recovery, focus or sleep. It costs $5.99 once and was #48 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 17 November.

item.title: Apple Health AI Study app: ask health questions, join in the US
item.description: Apple's new Apple Health AI Study app answers everyday health questions in plain language, with links to the medical research behind each answer. It's part of a US research study open to people 21 and older, with room for up to 200,000 participants.
